name: Jagathrakshaka Perumal Temple, Thirukkoodalur
deity: Vishnu as Jagathrakshaka Perumal — Vaiyam Katha Perumal, 'the lord who guards the world' — with the Goddess Padmasini (also called Pushpavalli)
period: A Divya Desam of the Chola country near the Kaveri, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
dynasty: Medieval Chola, with Vijayanagara and Nayak additions
summary: At Thirukkoodalur, between Thiruvaiyaru and Kumbakonam, Vishnu is worshipped as Jagathrakshaka — Vaiyam Katha Perumal, the guardian of the world — a Chola Nadu Divya Desam sung by Thirumangai Alvar.

sections.history: Thirukkoodalur, known locally as Aduthurai Perumal Koil, stands in the village of Vadakurangaduthurai between Thiruvaiyaru and Kumbakonam. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Chola Nadu, the Kaveri country. Its lord is Jagathrakshaka, in Tamil Vaiyam Katha Perumal — the one who keeps the whole world safe. The shrine is believed to have been founded under the Medieval Cholas around the late eighth century, with later contributions from the Vijayanagara kings and the Madurai Nayaks. Local tradition adds that an older temple was damaged by the floods of the Kaveri, and that the present one was raised by Rani Mangammal after the Lord appeared to her in a dream. The temple is administered today by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
sections.architecture: The temple is a compact Dravidian enclosure: a brick wall surrounds the precinct, gathering its shrines and sacred waters within, and a three-tiered rajagopuram marks the entrance. Over the sanctum of Jagathrakshaka rises the Suddha Satva Vimana, the 'tower of pure goodness'. The Goddess, worshipped as Padmasini, has her own shrine facing south. Behind the sanctum grows a jackfruit tree that the temple holds sacred, for tradition links it with the appearance of the Lord's conch.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that the Lord revealed himself here to the sage Nandaka and to King Ambarisha, the devoted ruler whose steadfast Ekadashi vow is remembered in the story of his trial by the sage Durvasa. The name Koodalur is linked with the Tamil word koodal, a gathering, and the shrine is also called Sangama Kshetram; it is sometimes styled the 'northern Koodalur' to set it apart from Koodal, the old name of Madurai. In his hymn Thirumangai Alvar calls the village 'Pugunthaan Oor' — the place the Lord entered — and the jackfruit tree behind the sanctum is believed to be where his conch appeared.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Sri Vaishnava calendar of the Kaveri country. Vaikunta Ekadashi in Margazhi (December–January) holds a special resonance at a shrine linked with Ambarisha, the king remembered for his Ekadashi vow, and processions of the utsava deity mark the festival days through the year. Ask the temple office for the current year's dates.
sections.experience: Thirukkoodalur is a quiet village temple, best visited unhurried. Walk the enclosure within the brick wall, pause before the south-facing shrine of Padmasini, and look for the jackfruit tree behind the sanctum. It pairs naturally with the nearby Divya Desam of Kapisthalam and with the Shiva temple of Vadakurangaduthurai in the same village, all along the Kaveri between Thiruvaiyaru and Kumbakonam.

visit.timings: Open daily for morning and evening darshan, with a midday closure; festival days are the busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is removed before entering. Follow posted rules and the guidance of the priests.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow posted rules and the guidance of the priests.
visit.gettingThere: Thirukkoodalur (Aduthurai) lies in the village of Vadakurangaduthurai in Thanjavur district, between Thiruvaiyaru and Kumbakonam, and is reached by road from either town. Kumbakonam and Thanjavur have the nearest major railway stations; Tiruchirappalli has the nearest airport.
